title: Electricity and Magnetism
topics: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A small body carries a charge of 3 electronic charges. Taking the elementary charge as 1.6 x 10^-19 C, calculate the charge on the body in units of 10^-19 C.
items.s: Charge = number of elementary charges x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 3 x 1.6 = 4.8 units of 10^-19 C.

items.q: Two parallel plates 0.1 m apart carry a uniform electric field of 400 V/m between them. Calculate the potential difference between the plates in V.
items.s: Potential difference = field intensity x separation = 400 x 0.1 = 40 V.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 50 microfarad is connected across a 250 V supply. Calculate the charge stored on it in microcoulomb.
items.s: Charge stored = capacitance x voltage = 50 x 10^-6 x 250 = 12500 microcoulomb.

items.q: Three capacitors of 2 microfarad, 6 microfarad and 3 microfarad are joined in parallel. Calculate the equivalent capacitance in microfarad.
items.s: Capacitors in parallel add directly, so the equivalent capacitance is 2 + 6 + 3 = 11 microfarad.

items.q: A resistor of 5 ohm is connected across a 48 V supply of negligible internal resistance. Calculate the current through it in A.
items.s: Current = voltage / resistance = 48 / 5 = 9.6 A.

items.q: Resistors of 8 ohm, 10 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistances in series add directly, so the total is 8 + 10 + 15 = 33 ohm.

items.q: A device draws a current of 2.5 A from a 12 V supply. Calculate the power it consumes in W.
items.s: Power = voltage x current = 12 x 2.5 = 30 W.

items.q: A straight wire of length 0.5 m carries a current of 1 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.6 T. Calculate the force on the wire in N.
items.s: Force = flux density x current x length = 0.6 x 1 x 0.5 = 0.3 N.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: An alternating current has a peak value of 10 A. Calculate its root mean square value in A.
items.s: The root mean square value is the peak value divided by the square root of two = 10 / 1.414 = 7.07 A.

items.q: Two point charges of 8 microcoulomb and 2 microcoulomb are placed 0.4 m apart in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the force between them in N.
items.s: Force = constant x product of the charges / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 8 x 10^-6 x 2 x 10^-6 / (0.4 x 0.4) = 0.9 N.

items.q: A point charge of 8 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.4 m from it in kV/m.
items.s: Field intensity = constant x charge / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 8 x 10^-6 / (0.4 x 0.4) = 450 kV/m.

items.q: A point charge of 4 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric potential 0.6 m from it in kV.
items.s: Potential = constant x charge / distance = 9.0 x 10^9 x 4 x 10^-6 / 0.6 = 60 kV.

items.q: A charge of 20 microcoulomb is moved between two points whose potential difference is 200 V. Calculate the work done in mJ.
items.s: Work done = charge x potential difference = 20 x 10^-6 x 200 = 4 mJ.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 4 microfarad is charged to 250 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.
items.s: Energy stored = half the capacitance times the voltage squared = 0.5 x 4 x 10^-6 x 250 x 250 = 125 mJ.

items.q: Two capacitors of 12 microfarad and 24 microfarad are connected in series. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination in microfarad.
items.s: For capacitors in series the reciprocals add, so the equivalent capacitance is 12 x 24 / (12 + 24) = 8 microfarad.

items.q: Two resistors of 6 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in parallel. Calculate their combined resistance in ohm.
items.s: For two resistors in parallel the combined value is 6 x 12 / (6 + 12) = 4 ohm.

items.q: A cell of electromotive force 3 V and internal resistance 0.8 ohm delivers a current of 1.5 A. Calculate its terminal potential difference in V.
items.s: Terminal voltage = electromotive force - current x internal resistance = 3 - 1.5 x 0.8 = 1.8 V.

items.q: A wire of length 4 m and cross sectional area 1 x 10^-6 m squared is made of a material of resistivity 10 x 10^-8 ohm m. Calculate its resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistance = resistivity x length / area = 10 x 10^-8 x 4 / (1 x 10^-6) = 0.4 ohm.

items.q: A current of 2 A divides between two parallel resistors of 10 ohm and 6 ohm. Calculate the current through the 10 ohm resistor in A.
items.s: The current divides in inverse proportion to the resistances, so through the 10 ohm branch it is 2 x 6 / (10 + 6) = 0.75 A.

items.q: A current of 4 A flows through a resistor of 20 ohm. Calculate the rate at which heat is produced in it in W.
items.s: Rate of heating = current squared x resistance = 4 x 4 x 20 = 320 W.

items.q: An appliance rated 3000 W is used for 3 hours. Calculate the energy it consumes in kWh.
items.s: Energy = power x time = 3000 W x 3 h = 9 kWh after dividing by one thousand.

items.q: A heater rated 2000 W runs for 3 hours each day. If electrical energy costs 40 naira per kWh, calculate the daily cost in naira.
items.s: The daily energy is 2000 x 3 / 1000 = 6 kWh, so the cost is 6 x 40 = 240 naira.

items.q: A flat surface of area 0.04 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.6 T. Calculate the magnetic flux through the surface in Wb.
items.s: Flux = flux density x area for a surface at right angles = 0.6 x 0.04 = 0.024 Wb.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current of 5 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the magnetic flux density 0.15 m from the wire in microtesla.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x current / (2 pi x distance) = 6.67 microtesla.

items.q: A solenoid of length 0.5 m has 800 turns and carries a current of 4 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density near its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x turns per metre x current = 8.04 mT.

items.q: A circular coil of 50 turns and radius 0.05 m carries a current of 4 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density at its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density at the centre = permeability x turns x current / (2 x radius) = 2.51 mT.

items.q: A particle carrying 6 microcoulomb moves at 10 x 10^6 m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T. Calculate the magnetic force on it in N.
items.s: Force = charge x speed x flux density for motion at right angles = 6 x 10^-6 x 10 x 10^6 x 0.5 = 30 N.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A coil of 400 turns and area 0.05 m squared carries a current of 3 A with its plane along a magnetic field of flux density 1 T. Calculate the turning effect on the coil in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = turns x current x area x flux density = 400 x 3 x 0.05 x 1 = 60 N m.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A coil of 200 turns and area 0.1 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field that changes uniformly from 0.2 T to 0.5 T in 1 s. Calculate the average voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = turns x change of flux density x area / time = 200 x 0.3 x 0.1 / 1 = 6 V.

items.q: A transformer has 1000 turns in its primary and 40 turns in its secondary. If the primary is connected to a 24 V supply, calculate the secondary voltage in V.
items.s: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, so the secondary voltage is 24 x 40 / 1000 = 0.96 V.

items.q: An ideal transformer has 400 primary turns and 500 secondary turns and the primary current is 1 A. Calculate the secondary current in A.
items.s: For an ideal transformer the current ratio is the inverse of the turns ratio, so the secondary current is 1 x 400 / 500 = 0.8 A.

items.q: The current in a coil of inductance 0.2 H changes steadily by 2 A in 0.1 s. Calculate the voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = inductance x rate of change of current = 0.2 x 2 / 0.1 = 4 V.

items.q: An alternating current has a peak value of 2 A. Calculate its root mean square value in A.
items.s: The root mean square value is the peak value divided by the square root of two = 2 / 1.414 = 1.41 A.

items.q: A capacitor of 20 microfarad is connected to a 100 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its capacitive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Capacitive reactance = 1 / (2 pi x frequency x capacitance) = 1 / (2 x 3.142 x 100 x 20 x 10^-6) = 79.57 ohm.

items.q: A coil of inductance 0.5 H is connected to a 200 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its inductive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Inductive reactance = 2 pi x frequency x inductance = 2 x 3.142 x 200 x 0.5 = 628.4 ohm.

items.q: A series circuit contains a resistance of 12 ohm and a reactance of 12 ohm. Calculate its impedance in ohm.
items.s: Impedance is the square root of the sum of the squares = sqrt(12 x 12 + 12 x 12) = 16.97 ohm.

items.q: A series circuit contains an inductance of 1 H and a capacitance of 2 microfarad. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its resonant frequency in Hz.
items.s: At resonance the frequency is 1 / (2 pi x square root of inductance x capacitance) = 112.5 Hz.

items.q: A circuit draws a root mean square current of 0.5 A from a 120 V root mean square supply at a power factor of 0.6. Calculate the true power consumed in W.
items.s: True power = voltage x current x power factor = 120 x 0.5 x 0.6 = 36 W.

items.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge the first arm is 12 ohm, the second is 2 ohm and the third is 8 ohm. Calculate the resistance of the fourth arm in ohm.
items.s: At balance the ratio of the first two arms equals the ratio of the last two, so the fourth arm is 2 x 8 / 12 = 1.33 ohm.

items.q: A metre bridge balances with a resistance of 4 ohm in the left gap and a balance length of 30 cm from the left end. Calculate the unknown resistance in the right gap in ohm.
items.s: The unknown equals the known resistance times the balance length divided by the remaining length = 4 x 30 / 70 = 1.71 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.1 A. Calculate the shunt needed to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 0.5 A, in ohm.
items.s: The shunt carries the excess current, so its value is 50 x 0.1 / (0.5 - 0.1) = 12.5 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 25 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.002 A. Calculate the series resistance needed to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to 10 V, in ohm.
items.s: The series resistance must drop the remaining voltage, so its value is 10 / 0.002 - 25 = 4975 ohm.

items.q: Two point charges attract each other with a force of 5 N when they are a certain distance apart. Calculate the force in N when the separation is increased to 5 times its original value.
items.s: The force varies inversely as the square of the separation, so the new force is 5 divided by 5 x 5 = 0.2 N.

items.q: A small body carries a charge of 12 electronic charges. Taking the elementary charge as 1.6 x 10^-19 C, calculate the charge on the body in units of 10^-19 C.
items.s: Charge = number of elementary charges x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 12 x 1.6 = 19.2 units of 10^-19 C.

items.q: Two parallel plates 0.005 m apart carry a uniform electric field of 2000 V/m between them. Calculate the potential difference between the plates in V.
items.s: Potential difference = field intensity x separation = 2000 x 0.005 = 10 V.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 4 microfarad is connected across a 250 V supply. Calculate the charge stored on it in microcoulomb.
items.s: Charge stored = capacitance x voltage = 4 x 10^-6 x 250 = 1000 microcoulomb.

items.q: Three capacitors of 2 microfarad, 6 microfarad and 5 microfarad are joined in parallel. Calculate the equivalent capacitance in microfarad.
items.s: Capacitors in parallel add directly, so the equivalent capacitance is 2 + 6 + 5 = 13 microfarad.

items.q: A resistor of 20 ohm is connected across a 9 V supply of negligible internal resistance. Calculate the current through it in A.
items.s: Current = voltage / resistance = 9 / 20 = 0.45 A.

items.q: Resistors of 20 ohm, 6 ohm and 30 ohm are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistances in series add directly, so the total is 20 + 6 + 30 = 56 ohm.

items.q: A straight wire of length 0.25 m carries a current of 1 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.25 T. Calculate the force on the wire in N.
items.s: Force = flux density x current x length = 0.25 x 1 x 0.25 = 0.0625 N.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: An alternating current has a peak value of 14 A. Calculate its root mean square value in A.
items.s: The root mean square value is the peak value divided by the square root of two = 14 / 1.414 = 9.9 A.

items.q: Two point charges of 3 microcoulomb and 6 microcoulomb are placed 0.2 m apart in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the force between them in N.
items.s: Force = constant x product of the charges / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 3 x 10^-6 x 6 x 10^-6 / (0.2 x 0.2) = 4.05 N.

items.q: A point charge of 1 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.3 m from it in kV/m.
items.s: Field intensity = constant x charge / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 1 x 10^-6 / (0.3 x 0.3) = 100 kV/m.

items.q: A point charge of 1 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric potential 0.1 m from it in kV.
items.s: Potential = constant x charge / distance = 9.0 x 10^9 x 1 x 10^-6 / 0.1 = 90 kV.

items.q: A charge of 4 microcoulomb is moved between two points whose potential difference is 50 V. Calculate the work done in mJ.
items.s: Work done = charge x potential difference = 4 x 10^-6 x 50 = 0.2 mJ.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 2 microfarad is charged to 200 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.
items.s: Energy stored = half the capacitance times the voltage squared = 0.5 x 2 x 10^-6 x 200 x 200 = 40 mJ.

items.q: Two capacitors of 8 microfarad and 16 microfarad are connected in series. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination in microfarad.
items.s: For capacitors in series the reciprocals add, so the equivalent capacitance is 8 x 16 / (8 + 16) = 5.33 microfarad.

items.q: Two resistors of 8 ohm and 24 ohm are connected in parallel. Calculate their combined resistance in ohm.
items.s: For two resistors in parallel the combined value is 8 x 24 / (8 + 24) = 6 ohm.

items.q: A cell of electromotive force 24 V and internal resistance 0.2 ohm delivers a current of 1.5 A. Calculate its terminal potential difference in V.
items.s: Terminal voltage = electromotive force - current x internal resistance = 24 - 1.5 x 0.2 = 23.7 V.

items.q: A wire of length 2 m and cross sectional area 0.5 x 10^-6 m squared is made of a material of resistivity 10 x 10^-8 ohm m. Calculate its resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistance = resistivity x length / area = 10 x 10^-8 x 2 / (0.5 x 10^-6) = 0.4 ohm.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines equipotential surface?
o: a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge
the work accumulated in a charged device, equal to half the product of its capacitance and the square of the voltage
the push per unit positive charge experienced at a point in a region of electrical influence
the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region
items.s: equipotential surface: a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge. The other options describe torque on a coil, electric field intensity, energy stored in a capacitor.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines energy dissipated?
o: the lead or lag between the voltage across a circuit and the current through it
the rule that the voltage across a conductor is proportional to the current through it at constant temperature
the product of the influence through one turn of a coil and the number of turns
the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component
items.s: energy dissipated: the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component. The other options describe phase angle, ohm law of conduction, magnetic flux linkage.

items.q: ammeter may be defined as
o: a high resistance placed in series with an instrument to extend the range of voltage it can read
a four arm network balanced when the ratio of two pairs of resistances is equal
an instrument connected in the line of a circuit to measure the rate of charge flow
a flow of charge that reverses its direction at regular intervals
items.s: ammeter: an instrument connected in the line of a circuit to measure the rate of charge flow. The other options describe multiplier, alternating current, Wheatstone bridge.

items.q: Which of the following best describes resistance?
o: the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component
the opposition a conductor offers to the flow of charge through it
the rule that the push between two point charges varies as the product of the charges and inversely as the squared separation
a convention relating the directions of push, flux density and current for a conductor placed across a magnetic region
items.s: resistance: the opposition a conductor offers to the flow of charge through it. The other options describe Fleming left hand rule, energy dissipated, Coulomb law of force.

items.q: Which term is described by “the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material”?
o: permittivity
electric charge
conservation of charge
electrostatic shielding
items.s: electrostatic shielding is the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material.

items.q: Which of the following best describes potential difference?
o: the condition in which the capacitive and inductive oppositions cancel so the current is greatest
the slow loss of stored charge through an imperfect insulator
the work done per unit charge in carrying charge between two points in a circuit
the rule that the push between two point charges varies as the product of the charges and inversely as the squared separation
items.s: potential difference: the work done per unit charge in carrying charge between two points in a circuit. The other options describe resonance, leakage, Coulomb law of force.

items.q: Which of the following best describes eddy current?
o: the rule that the induced voltage equals the rate of change of flux linkage
a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence
a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge
a flow of charge that reverses its direction at regular intervals
items.s: eddy current: a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence. The other options describe Faraday law of induction, alternating current, equipotential surface.

items.q: Coulomb law of force may be defined as
o: a substance such as iron that greatly concentrates the magnetic influence passing through it
the opposition to alternating current offered by a capacitor or a coil without dissipating energy
the rule that the push between two point charges varies as the product of the charges and inversely as the squared separation
a sensitive instrument that detects small currents by the swing of a coil in a magnetic region
items.s: Coulomb law of force: the rule that the push between two point charges varies as the product of the charges and inversely as the squared separation. The other options describe galvanometer, ferromagnetic material, reactance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes electric flux?
o: the number of lines of electrical influence crossing a stated area
a wiring in which the same voltage appears across every branch
a flow of charge that reverses its direction at regular intervals
the opposition inside a source that makes its terminal voltage fall as it delivers current
items.s: electric flux: the number of lines of electrical influence crossing a stated area. The other options describe internal resistance, parallel connection, alternating current.

items.q: Which term is described by “the opposition to alternating current offered by a capacitor or a coil without dissipating energy”?
o: alternating current
reactance
impedance
resonance
items.s: reactance is the opposition to alternating current offered by a capacitor or a coil without dissipating energy.

items.q: All of the following belong to Electric field and potential EXCEPT
o: electric field intensity
power factor
electric potential
potential difference
items.s: Every other option belongs to Electric field and potential. “power factor” belongs to Alternating current circuits, not Electric field and potential.

items.q: The statement “a long coil of insulated wire that produces a nearly uniform magnetic region inside it” describes which of the following?
o: right hand grip rule
solenoid
tesla
permeability
items.s: solenoid is a long coil of insulated wire that produces a nearly uniform magnetic region inside it.

items.q: The statement “the turning or pushing of a conductor carrying current when placed across a magnetic region” describes which of the following?
o: motor effect
force on a moving charge
torque on a coil
Fleming left hand rule
items.s: motor effect is the turning or pushing of a conductor carrying current when placed across a magnetic region.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: Which of the following best describes meter bridge?
o: the production of heat in a conductor by the passage of current through its resistance
the rate at which the energy per unit charge changes with distance along a direction
a practical form of balanced network using a one metre wire to find an unknown resistance
a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence
items.s: meter bridge: a practical form of balanced network using a one metre wire to find an unknown resistance. The other options describe potential gradient, joule heating, eddy current.

items.q: Which term is described by “a wiring in which the same current passes through every component one after another”?
o: resistance
ohm law of conduction
series connection
internal resistance
items.s: series connection is a wiring in which the same current passes through every component one after another.

items.q: The statement “the rate at which charge passes a given point in a circuit” describes which of the following?
o: electric current
resistivity
electromotive force
resistance
items.s: electric current is the rate at which charge passes a given point in a circuit.

items.q: Which of the following best describes field line?
o: a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the electric push there
the turning or pushing of a conductor carrying current when placed across a magnetic region
the opposition inside a source that makes its terminal voltage fall as it delivers current
a closed curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the push due to a magnet or a current
items.s: field line: a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the electric push there. The other options describe magnetic field line, motor effect, internal resistance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines field line?
o: a sensitive instrument that detects small currents by the swing of a coil in a magnetic region
a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the electric push there
the rate of energy transfer a device is designed to handle safely
a low resistance placed across an instrument to carry most of the current past it
items.s: field line: a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the electric push there. The other options describe power rating, galvanometer, shunt.

items.q: energy stored in a capacitor may be defined as
o: a wiring in which the same current passes through every component one after another
the inductance of a coil in which a current changing at one ampere per second induces one volt
the energy supplied per unit charge by a source as it drives charge round a circuit
the work accumulated in a charged device, equal to half the product of its capacitance and the square of the voltage
items.s: energy stored in a capacitor: the work accumulated in a charged device, equal to half the product of its capacitance and the square of the voltage. The other options describe henry, series connection, electromotive force.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines cyclotron motion?
o: the rate of energy transfer a device is designed to handle safely
a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge
the circular path followed by a charged particle entering a magnetic region at right angles
the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region
items.s: cyclotron motion: the circular path followed by a charged particle entering a magnetic region at right angles. The other options describe equipotential surface, power rating, torque on a coil.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: Which statement correctly defines electrostatic shielding?
o: the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material
the work accumulated in a charged device, equal to half the product of its capacitance and the square of the voltage
the opposition a conductor offers to the flow of charge through it
the combined push on a charge moving in regions of electric and magnetic influence
items.s: electrostatic shielding: the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material. The other options describe resistance, Lorentz force, energy stored in a capacitor.

items.q: magnetic flux density may be defined as
o: the slow loss of stored charge through an imperfect insulator
the force acting per unit length on a wire carrying unit current at right angles to the region
the rule that any observed amount of electricity on a body is a whole number multiple of the elementary amount
a substance such as iron that greatly concentrates the magnetic influence passing through it
items.s: magnetic flux density: the force acting per unit length on a wire carrying unit current at right angles to the region. The other options describe leakage, quantisation of charge, ferromagnetic material.

items.q: magnetic field may be defined as
o: a region in which a moving charge or a magnet experiences a sideways push
an instrument connected in the line of a circuit to measure the rate of charge flow
the rate of energy transfer a device is designed to handle safely
a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge
items.s: magnetic field: a region in which a moving charge or a magnet experiences a sideways push. The other options describe equipotential surface, power rating, ammeter.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines right hand grip rule?
o: the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region
the production of heat in a conductor by the passage of current through its resistance
the convention that a current held along the thumb of one limb gives lines of magnetic influence along the curled fingers
the rate of energy transfer a device is designed to handle safely
items.s: right hand grip rule: the convention that a current held along the thumb of one limb gives lines of magnetic influence along the curled fingers. The other options describe torque on a coil, joule heating, power rating.

items.q: The statement “a closed curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the push due to a magnet or a current” describes which of the following?
o: permeability
magnetic flux density
magnetic field line
right hand grip rule
items.s: magnetic field line is a closed curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the push due to a magnet or a current.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines resonance.
o: the condition in which the capacitive and inductive oppositions cancel so the current is greatest
the total opposition to alternating current from resistance and reactance together
two flat conducting sheets facing each other with an insulator between them, used to store charge
the combined push on a charge moving in regions of electric and magnetic influence
items.s: resonance: the condition in which the capacitive and inductive oppositions cancel so the current is greatest. The other options describe Lorentz force, impedance, parallel plate arrangement.

items.q: Which term is described by “the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region”?
o: Lorentz force
torque on a coil
force on a moving charge
galvanometer
items.s: torque on a coil is the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: energy dissipated may be defined as
o: a uniform wire and sliding contact used to compare voltages without drawing current from the source being measured
the transfer of charge to a conductor without any contact, by bringing a charged body near it
the rate of energy transfer a device is designed to handle safely
the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component
items.s: energy dissipated: the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component. The other options describe power rating, potentiometer, charging by induction.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines solenoid.
o: the lead or lag between the voltage across a circuit and the current through it
a closed curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the push due to a magnet or a current
the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to a point
a long coil of insulated wire that produces a nearly uniform magnetic region inside it
items.s: solenoid: a long coil of insulated wire that produces a nearly uniform magnetic region inside it. The other options describe phase angle, magnetic field line, electric potential.

items.q: The statement “the principle that electricity can be neither created nor destroyed within an isolated region” describes which of the following?
o: conservation of charge
electrostatic shielding
point charge
electric charge
items.s: conservation of charge is the principle that electricity can be neither created nor destroyed within an isolated region.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rate at which a circuit transfers energy, equal to the product of voltage and current”?
o: overload
joule heating
efficiency of a source
electrical power
items.s: electrical power is the rate at which a circuit transfers energy, equal to the product of voltage and current.

items.q: root mean square value may be defined as
o: the steady amount that would deliver the same heating as a varying quantity over a full cycle
the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region
the combined push on a charge moving in regions of electric and magnetic influence
a substance such as iron that greatly concentrates the magnetic influence passing through it
items.s: root mean square value: the steady amount that would deliver the same heating as a varying quantity over a full cycle. The other options describe Lorentz force, ferromagnetic material, torque on a coil.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines joule heating.
o: the circular path followed by a charged particle entering a magnetic region at right angles
the rate at which charge passes a given point in a circuit
the production of heat in a conductor by the passage of current through its resistance
the number of lines of electrical influence crossing a stated area

items.q: A point charge of 6 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.4 m from it in kV/m.
items.s: Field intensity = constant x charge / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 6 x 10^-6 / (0.4 x 0.4) = 337.5 kV/m.

items.q: A point charge of 4 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric potential 0.4 m from it in kV.
items.s: Potential = constant x charge / distance = 9.0 x 10^9 x 4 x 10^-6 / 0.4 = 90 kV.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 5 microfarad is charged to 240 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.
items.s: Energy stored = half the capacitance times the voltage squared = 0.5 x 5 x 10^-6 x 240 x 240 = 144 mJ.

items.q: Two resistors of 4 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in parallel. Calculate their combined resistance in ohm.
items.s: For two resistors in parallel the combined value is 4 x 12 / (4 + 12) = 3 ohm.

items.q: A cell of electromotive force 2 V and internal resistance 1.5 ohm delivers a current of 2 A. Calculate its terminal potential difference in V.
items.s: Terminal voltage = electromotive force - current x internal resistance = 2 - 2 x 1.5 = -1 V.

items.q: A current of 4 A flows through a resistor of 12 ohm. Calculate the rate at which heat is produced in it in W.
items.s: Rate of heating = current squared x resistance = 4 x 4 x 12 = 192 W.

items.q: An appliance rated 1000 W is used for 4 hours. Calculate the energy it consumes in kWh.
items.s: Energy = power x time = 1000 W x 4 h = 4 kWh after dividing by one thousand.

items.q: A flat surface of area 0.25 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T. Calculate the magnetic flux through the surface in Wb.
items.s: Flux = flux density x area for a surface at right angles = 0.5 x 0.25 = 0.125 Wb.

items.q: A coil of 20 turns and area 0.05 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field that changes uniformly from 0.1 T to 1 T in 0.5 s. Calculate the average voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = turns x change of flux density x area / time = 20 x 0.9 x 0.05 / 0.5 = 1.8 V.

items.q: A transformer has 1000 turns in its primary and 200 turns in its secondary. If the primary is connected to a 12 V supply, calculate the secondary voltage in V.
items.s: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, so the secondary voltage is 12 x 200 / 1000 = 2.4 V.

items.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge the first arm is 2 ohm, the second is 2 ohm and the third is 10 ohm. Calculate the resistance of the fourth arm in ohm.
items.s: At balance the ratio of the first two arms equals the ratio of the last two, so the fourth arm is 2 x 10 / 2 = 10 ohm.

items.q: Two point charges attract each other with a force of 12 N when they are a certain distance apart. Calculate the force in N when the separation is increased to 3 times its original value.
items.s: The force varies inversely as the square of the separation, so the new force is 12 divided by 3 x 3 = 1.33 N.

items.q: A small body carries a charge of 5 electronic charges. Taking the elementary charge as 1.6 x 10^-19 C, calculate the charge on the body in units of 10^-19 C.
items.s: Charge = number of elementary charges x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 5 x 1.6 = 8 units of 10^-19 C.

items.q: Two parallel plates 0.02 m apart carry a uniform electric field of 500 V/m between them. Calculate the potential difference between the plates in V.
items.s: Potential difference = field intensity x separation = 500 x 0.02 = 10 V.

items.q: A charge of 25 microcoulomb is moved between two points whose potential difference is 500 V. Calculate the work done in mJ.
items.s: Work done = charge x potential difference = 25 x 10^-6 x 500 = 12.5 mJ.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 20 microfarad is connected across a 50 V supply. Calculate the charge stored on it in microcoulomb.
items.s: Charge stored = capacitance x voltage = 20 x 10^-6 x 50 = 1000 microcoulomb.

items.q: Two capacitors of 8 microfarad and 24 microfarad are connected in series. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination in microfarad.
items.s: For capacitors in series the reciprocals add, so the equivalent capacitance is 8 x 24 / (8 + 24) = 6 microfarad.

items.q: Three capacitors of 2 microfarad, 6 microfarad and 6 microfarad are joined in parallel. Calculate the equivalent capacitance in microfarad.
items.s: Capacitors in parallel add directly, so the equivalent capacitance is 2 + 6 + 6 = 14 microfarad.

items.q: A resistor of 15 ohm is connected across a 6 V supply of negligible internal resistance. Calculate the current through it in A.
items.s: Current = voltage / resistance = 6 / 15 = 0.4 A.

items.q: Resistors of 20 ohm, 2 ohm and 10 ohm are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistances in series add directly, so the total is 20 + 2 + 10 = 32 ohm.

items.q: A wire of length 1 m and cross sectional area 0.2 x 10^-6 m squared is made of a material of resistivity 4.9 x 10^-8 ohm m. Calculate its resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistance = resistivity x length / area = 4.9 x 10^-8 x 1 / (0.2 x 10^-6) = 0.245 ohm.

items.q: A current of 2 A divides between two parallel resistors of 8 ohm and 4 ohm. Calculate the current through the 8 ohm resistor in A.
items.s: The current divides in inverse proportion to the resistances, so through the 8 ohm branch it is 2 x 4 / (8 + 4) = 0.6667 A.

items.q: A device draws a current of 2.5 A from a 24 V supply. Calculate the power it consumes in W.
items.s: Power = voltage x current = 24 x 2.5 = 60 W.

items.q: A heater rated 1500 W runs for 3 hours each day. If electrical energy costs 40 naira per kWh, calculate the daily cost in naira.
items.s: The daily energy is 1500 x 3 / 1000 = 4.5 kWh, so the cost is 4.5 x 40 = 180 naira.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current of 15 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the magnetic flux density 0.15 m from the wire in microtesla.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x current / (2 pi x distance) = 20 microtesla.

items.q: A solenoid of length 0.5 m has 1500 turns and carries a current of 1 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density near its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x turns per metre x current = 3.77 mT.

items.q: A circular coil of 50 turns and radius 0.05 m carries a current of 0.5 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density at its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density at the centre = permeability x turns x current / (2 x radius) = 0.3142 mT.

items.q: A straight wire of length 0.2 m carries a current of 5 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.8 T. Calculate the force on the wire in N.
items.s: Force = flux density x current x length = 0.8 x 5 x 0.2 = 0.8 N.

items.q: A particle carrying 2 microcoulomb moves at 2 x 10^6 m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T. Calculate the magnetic force on it in N.

items.q: A coil of 200 turns and area 0.1 m squared carries a current of 1.5 A with its plane along a magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T. Calculate the turning effect on the coil in N m.

items.q: An ideal transformer has 400 primary turns and 20 secondary turns and the primary current is 3 A. Calculate the secondary current in A.
items.s: For an ideal transformer the current ratio is the inverse of the turns ratio, so the secondary current is 3 x 400 / 20 = 60 A.

items.q: The current in a coil of inductance 1 H changes steadily by 1.5 A in 0.1 s. Calculate the voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = inductance x rate of change of current = 1 x 1.5 / 0.1 = 15 V.

items.q: An alternating current has a peak value of 6 A. Calculate its root mean square value in A.
items.s: The root mean square value is the peak value divided by the square root of two = 6 / 1.414 = 4.24 A.

items.q: A capacitor of 25 microfarad is connected to a 60 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its capacitive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Capacitive reactance = 1 / (2 pi x frequency x capacitance) = 1 / (2 x 3.142 x 60 x 25 x 10^-6) = 106.1 ohm.

items.q: A coil of inductance 1.5 H is connected to a 100 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its inductive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Inductive reactance = 2 pi x frequency x inductance = 2 x 3.142 x 100 x 1.5 = 942.6 ohm.

items.q: A series circuit contains a resistance of 5 ohm and a reactance of 8 ohm. Calculate its impedance in ohm.
items.s: Impedance is the square root of the sum of the squares = sqrt(5 x 5 + 8 x 8) = 9.43 ohm.

items.q: A series circuit contains an inductance of 0.25 H and a capacitance of 50 microfarad. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its resonant frequency in Hz.
items.s: At resonance the frequency is 1 / (2 pi x square root of inductance x capacitance) = 45.01 Hz.

items.q: A circuit draws a root mean square current of 5 A from a 220 V root mean square supply at a power factor of 0.75. Calculate the true power consumed in W.
items.s: True power = voltage x current x power factor = 220 x 5 x 0.75 = 825 W.

items.q: A metre bridge balances with a resistance of 8 ohm in the left gap and a balance length of 25 cm from the left end. Calculate the unknown resistance in the right gap in ohm.
items.s: The unknown equals the known resistance times the balance length divided by the remaining length = 8 x 25 / 75 = 2.67 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 20 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.05 A. Calculate the shunt needed to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 1 A, in ohm.
items.s: The shunt carries the excess current, so its value is 20 x 0.05 / (1 - 0.05) = 1.05 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 25 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.005 A. Calculate the series resistance needed to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to 50 V, in ohm.

items.q: Two point charges of 4 microcoulomb and 1 microcoulomb are placed 0.5 m apart in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the force between them in N.

items.q: A point charge of 6 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.1 m from it in kV/m.

items.q: A point charge of 8 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric potential 0.25 m from it in kV.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 5 microfarad is charged to 50 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.

items.q: Two resistors of 4 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Calculate their combined resistance in ohm.

items.q: A cell of electromotive force 4.5 V and internal resistance 0.2 ohm delivers a current of 0.5 A. Calculate its terminal potential difference in V.

items.q: A current of 2.5 A flows through a resistor of 10 ohm. Calculate the rate at which heat is produced in it in W.

items.q: A coil of 100 turns and area 0.02 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field that changes uniformly from 0 T to 0.8 T in 1 s. Calculate the average voltage induced in the coil in V.

items.q: A transformer has 100 turns in its primary and 200 turns in its secondary. If the primary is connected to a 220 V supply, calculate the secondary voltage in V.

items.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge the first arm is 5 ohm, the second is 12 ohm and the third is 20 ohm. Calculate the resistance of the fourth arm in ohm.

items.q: Two capacitors of 4 microfarad and 12 microfarad are connected in series. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination in microfarad.

items.q: A wire of length 1.5 m and cross sectional area 0.2 x 10^-6 m squared is made of a material of resistivity 4.9 x 10^-8 ohm m. Calculate its resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistance = resistivity x length / area = 4.9 x 10^-8 x 1.5 / (0.2 x 10^-6) = 0.3675 ohm.

items.q: A current of 3 A divides between two parallel resistors of 8 ohm and 12 ohm. Calculate the current through the 8 ohm resistor in A.
items.s: The current divides in inverse proportion to the resistances, so through the 8 ohm branch it is 3 x 12 / (8 + 12) = 1.8 A.

items.q: A heater rated 1500 W runs for 6 hours each day. If electrical energy costs 25 naira per kWh, calculate the daily cost in naira.
items.s: The daily energy is 1500 x 6 / 1000 = 9 kWh, so the cost is 9 x 25 = 225 naira.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current of 20 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the magnetic flux density 0.2 m from the wire in microtesla.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x current / (2 pi x distance) = 20 microtesla.

items.q: A solenoid of length 0.2 m has 1500 turns and carries a current of 1.5 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density near its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x turns per metre x current = 14.14 mT.

items.q: A particle carrying 3 microcoulomb moves at 5 x 10^6 m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.4 T. Calculate the magnetic force on it in N.
items.s: Force = charge x speed x flux density for motion at right angles = 3 x 10^-6 x 5 x 10^6 x 0.4 = 6 N.

items.q: An ideal transformer has 200 primary turns and 100 secondary turns and the primary current is 1 A. Calculate the secondary current in A.
items.s: For an ideal transformer the current ratio is the inverse of the turns ratio, so the secondary current is 1 x 200 / 100 = 2 A.

items.q: The current in a coil of inductance 2.5 H changes steadily by 1 A in 0.2 s. Calculate the voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = inductance x rate of change of current = 2.5 x 1 / 0.2 = 12.5 V.

items.q: A capacitor of 1 microfarad is connected to a 500 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its capacitive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Capacitive reactance = 1 / (2 pi x frequency x capacitance) = 1 / (2 x 3.142 x 500 x 1 x 10^-6) = 318.3 ohm.

items.q: A coil of inductance 0.1 H is connected to a 500 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its inductive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Inductive reactance = 2 pi x frequency x inductance = 2 x 3.142 x 500 x 0.1 = 314.2 ohm.

items.q: A series circuit contains a resistance of 5 ohm and a reactance of 12 ohm. Calculate its impedance in ohm.
items.s: Impedance is the square root of the sum of the squares = sqrt(5 x 5 + 12 x 12) = 13 ohm.

items.q: A metre bridge balances with a resistance of 2 ohm in the left gap and a balance length of 60 cm from the left end. Calculate the unknown resistance in the right gap in ohm.
items.s: The unknown equals the known resistance times the balance length divided by the remaining length = 2 x 60 / 40 = 3 ohm.

items.q: Two point charges attract each other with a force of 10 N when they are a certain distance apart. Calculate the force in N when the separation is increased to 4 times its original value.
items.s: The force varies inversely as the square of the separation, so the new force is 10 divided by 4 x 4 = 0.625 N.

items.q: Two point charges of 5 microcoulomb and 4 microcoulomb are placed 0.1 m apart in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the force between them in N.
items.s: Force = constant x product of the charges / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 5 x 10^-6 x 4 x 10^-6 / (0.1 x 0.1) = 18 N.

items.q: A point charge of 10 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.2 m from it in kV/m.
items.s: Field intensity = constant x charge / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 10 x 10^-6 / (0.2 x 0.2) = 2250 kV/m.

items.q: A point charge of 8 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric potential 0.3 m from it in kV.
items.s: Potential = constant x charge / distance = 9.0 x 10^9 x 8 x 10^-6 / 0.3 = 240 kV.

items.q: Two parallel plates 0.2 m apart carry a uniform electric field of 500 V/m between them. Calculate the potential difference between the plates in V.
items.s: Potential difference = field intensity x separation = 500 x 0.2 = 100 V.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 4 microfarad is connected across a 100 V supply. Calculate the charge stored on it in microcoulomb.
items.s: Charge stored = capacitance x voltage = 4 x 10^-6 x 100 = 400 microcoulomb.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 20 microfarad is charged to 250 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.
items.s: Energy stored = half the capacitance times the voltage squared = 0.5 x 20 x 10^-6 x 250 x 250 = 625 mJ.

items.q: Three capacitors of 3 microfarad, 12 microfarad and 10 microfarad are joined in parallel. Calculate the equivalent capacitance in microfarad.
items.s: Capacitors in parallel add directly, so the equivalent capacitance is 3 + 12 + 10 = 25 microfarad.

items.q: A resistor of 6 ohm is connected across a 12 V supply of negligible internal resistance. Calculate the current through it in A.
items.s: Current = voltage / resistance = 12 / 6 = 2 A.

items.q: Resistors of 10 ohm, 2 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistances in series add directly, so the total is 10 + 2 + 12 = 24 ohm.

items.q: Two resistors of 12 ohm and 4 ohm are connected in parallel. Calculate their combined resistance in ohm.
items.s: For two resistors in parallel the combined value is 12 x 4 / (12 + 4) = 3 ohm.

items.q: A cell of electromotive force 4.5 V and internal resistance 1 ohm delivers a current of 2 A. Calculate its terminal potential difference in V.
items.s: Terminal voltage = electromotive force - current x internal resistance = 4.5 - 2 x 1 = 2.5 V.

items.q: A device draws a current of 2.5 A from a 240 V supply. Calculate the power it consumes in W.
items.s: Power = voltage x current = 240 x 2.5 = 600 W.

items.q: A current of 3 A flows through a resistor of 20 ohm. Calculate the rate at which heat is produced in it in W.
items.s: Rate of heating = current squared x resistance = 3 x 3 x 20 = 180 W.

items.q: An appliance rated 500 W is used for 3 hours. Calculate the energy it consumes in kWh.
items.s: Energy = power x time = 500 W x 3 h = 1.5 kWh after dividing by one thousand.

items.q: A flat surface of area 0.01 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.8 T. Calculate the magnetic flux through the surface in Wb.
items.s: Flux = flux density x area for a surface at right angles = 0.8 x 0.01 = 0.008 Wb.

items.q: A circular coil of 500 turns and radius 0.2 m carries a current of 4 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density at its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density at the centre = permeability x turns x current / (2 x radius) = 6.28 mT.

items.q: A straight wire of length 0.1 m carries a current of 1 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.4 T. Calculate the force on the wire in N.
items.s: Force = flux density x current x length = 0.4 x 1 x 0.1 = 0.04 N.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A coil of 400 turns and area 0.01 m squared carries a current of 1.5 A with its plane along a magnetic field of flux density 0.2 T. Calculate the turning effect on the coil in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = turns x current x area x flux density = 400 x 1.5 x 0.01 x 0.2 = 1.2 N m.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A coil of 500 turns and area 0.04 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field that changes uniformly from 0.1 T to 0.5 T in 0.5 s. Calculate the average voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = turns x change of flux density x area / time = 500 x 0.4 x 0.04 / 0.5 = 16 V.

items.q: A transformer has 1000 turns in its primary and 40 turns in its secondary. If the primary is connected to a 220 V supply, calculate the secondary voltage in V.
items.s: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, so the secondary voltage is 220 x 40 / 1000 = 8.8 V.

items.q: An alternating current has a peak value of 20 A. Calculate its root mean square value in A.
items.s: The root mean square value is the peak value divided by the square root of two = 20 / 1.414 = 14.14 A.

items.q: A series circuit contains an inductance of 0.1 H and a capacitance of 100 microfarad. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its resonant frequency in Hz.
items.s: At resonance the frequency is 1 / (2 pi x square root of inductance x capacitance) = 50.32 Hz.

items.q: A circuit draws a root mean square current of 1 A from a 220 V root mean square supply at a power factor of 0.85. Calculate the true power consumed in W.
items.s: True power = voltage x current x power factor = 220 x 1 x 0.85 = 187 W.

items.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge the first arm is 4 ohm, the second is 6 ohm and the third is 10 ohm. Calculate the resistance of the fourth arm in ohm.
items.s: At balance the ratio of the first two arms equals the ratio of the last two, so the fourth arm is 6 x 10 / 4 = 15 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 100 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.01 A. Calculate the shunt needed to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 2 A, in ohm.
items.s: The shunt carries the excess current, so its value is 100 x 0.01 / (2 - 0.01) = 0.5025 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.005 A. Calculate the series resistance needed to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to 5 V, in ohm.
items.s: The series resistance must drop the remaining voltage, so its value is 5 / 0.005 - 50 = 950 ohm.

items.q: A charge of 25 microcoulomb is moved between two points whose potential difference is 200 V. Calculate the work done in mJ.
items.s: Work done = charge x potential difference = 25 x 10^-6 x 200 = 5 mJ.

items.q: Two capacitors of 6 microfarad and 3 microfarad are connected in series. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination in microfarad.
items.s: For capacitors in series the reciprocals add, so the equivalent capacitance is 6 x 3 / (6 + 3) = 2 microfarad.

items.q: A wire of length 1.5 m and cross sectional area 1.5 x 10^-6 m squared is made of a material of resistivity 2.4 x 10^-8 ohm m. Calculate its resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistance = resistivity x length / area = 2.4 x 10^-8 x 1.5 / (1.5 x 10^-6) = 0.024 ohm.

items.q: A current of 2 A divides between two parallel resistors of 3 ohm and 2 ohm. Calculate the current through the 3 ohm resistor in A.
items.s: The current divides in inverse proportion to the resistances, so through the 3 ohm branch it is 2 x 2 / (3 + 2) = 0.8 A.

items.q: A heater rated 2000 W runs for 8 hours each day. If electrical energy costs 20 naira per kWh, calculate the daily cost in naira.
items.s: The daily energy is 2000 x 8 / 1000 = 16 kWh, so the cost is 16 x 20 = 320 naira.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current of 20 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the magnetic flux density 0.25 m from the wire in microtesla.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x current / (2 pi x distance) = 16 microtesla.

items.q: A solenoid of length 0.25 m has 200 turns and carries a current of 1 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density near its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x turns per metre x current = 1.01 mT.

items.q: A particle carrying 3 microcoulomb moves at 4 x 10^6 m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.2 T. Calculate the magnetic force on it in N.
items.s: Force = charge x speed x flux density for motion at right angles = 3 x 10^-6 x 4 x 10^6 x 0.2 = 2.4 N.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: An ideal transformer has 400 primary turns and 50 secondary turns and the primary current is 0.5 A. Calculate the secondary current in A.
items.s: For an ideal transformer the current ratio is the inverse of the turns ratio, so the secondary current is 0.5 x 400 / 50 = 4 A.

items.q: The current in a coil of inductance 0.8 H changes steadily by 0.5 A in 1 s. Calculate the voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = inductance x rate of change of current = 0.8 x 0.5 / 1 = 0.4 V.

items.q: A capacitor of 2 microfarad is connected to a 200 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its capacitive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Capacitive reactance = 1 / (2 pi x frequency x capacitance) = 1 / (2 x 3.142 x 200 x 2 x 10^-6) = 397.8 ohm.

items.q: A metre bridge balances with a resistance of 8 ohm in the left gap and a balance length of 65 cm from the left end. Calculate the unknown resistance in the right gap in ohm.
items.s: The unknown equals the known resistance times the balance length divided by the remaining length = 8 x 65 / 35 = 14.86 ohm.

items.q: Two point charges attract each other with a force of 8 N when they are a certain distance apart. Calculate the force in N when the separation is increased to 2 times its original value.
items.s: The force varies inversely as the square of the separation, so the new force is 8 divided by 2 x 2 = 2 N.

items.q: Two point charges of 6 microcoulomb and 3 microcoulomb are placed 0.5 m apart in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the force between them in N.
items.s: Force = constant x product of the charges / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 6 x 10^-6 x 3 x 10^-6 / (0.5 x 0.5) = 0.648 N.

items.q: A small body carries a charge of 8 electronic charges. Taking the elementary charge as 1.6 x 10^-19 C, calculate the charge on the body in units of 10^-19 C.
items.s: Charge = number of elementary charges x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 8 x 1.6 = 12.8 units of 10^-19 C.

items.q: A point charge of 3 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.1 m from it in kV/m.
items.s: Field intensity = constant x charge / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 3 x 10^-6 / (0.1 x 0.1) = 2700 kV/m.

items.q: A point charge of 8 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric potential 0.5 m from it in kV.
items.s: Potential = constant x charge / distance = 9.0 x 10^9 x 8 x 10^-6 / 0.5 = 144 kV.

items.q: Two parallel plates 0.2 m apart carry a uniform electric field of 200 V/m between them. Calculate the potential difference between the plates in V.
items.s: Potential difference = field intensity x separation = 200 x 0.2 = 40 V.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 8 microfarad is connected across a 24 V supply. Calculate the charge stored on it in microcoulomb.
items.s: Charge stored = capacitance x voltage = 8 x 10^-6 x 24 = 192 microcoulomb.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 5 microfarad is charged to 120 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.
items.s: Energy stored = half the capacitance times the voltage squared = 0.5 x 5 x 10^-6 x 120 x 120 = 36 mJ.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Faraday law of induction.
o: the rule that an induced current flows in the direction that opposes the change producing it
the product of the influence through one turn of a coil and the number of turns
a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence
the rule that the induced voltage equals the rate of change of flux linkage
items.s: Faraday law of induction: the rule that the induced voltage equals the rate of change of flux linkage. The other options describe magnetic flux linkage, Lenz law, eddy current.

items.q: energy dissipated is best described as
o: the condition in which a circuit carries more current than its components can safely bear
the ratio of the energy delivered to the load to the total energy generated
the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component
the rate at which a circuit transfers energy, equal to the product of voltage and current
items.s: energy dissipated: the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component. The other options describe electrical power, overload, efficiency of a source.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the energy supplied per unit charge by a source as it drives charge round a circuit”
o: resistivity
internal resistance
electromotive force
ohm law of conduction
items.s: electromotive force is the energy supplied per unit charge by a source as it drives charge round a circuit.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material”
o: electric charge
electrostatic shielding
permittivity
point charge
items.s: electrostatic shielding is the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a basic property of matter that makes a body attract or repel another and comes in two kinds”
o: electrostatic shielding
conservation of charge
permittivity
electric charge
items.s: electric charge is a basic property of matter that makes a body attract or repel another and comes in two kinds.

items.q: equivalent capacitance may be defined as
o: the single value that could replace a whole network between two terminals
the constant appearing in the law of force between charges in a vacuum
the capacitance of a conductor that holds one coulomb when its energy per unit charge rises by one volt
the slow loss of stored charge through an imperfect insulator
items.s: equivalent capacitance: the single value that could replace a whole network between two terminals. The other options describe leakage, permittivity of free space, farad.

items.q: Which of the following best describes charging by induction?
o: the rule that any observed amount of electricity on a body is a whole number multiple of the elementary amount
a basic property of matter that makes a body attract or repel another and comes in two kinds
the transfer of charge to a conductor without any contact, by bringing a charged body near it
a charged body whose size is negligible compared with the distances in the problem
items.s: charging by induction: the transfer of charge to a conductor without any contact, by bringing a charged body near it. The other options describe electric charge, quantisation of charge, point charge.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Electric charge and Coulomb force?
o: quantisation of charge
Lorentz force
electric charge
conservation of charge
items.s: Every other option belongs to Electric charge and Coulomb force. “Lorentz force” belongs to Force on a current in a magnetic field, not Electric charge and Coulomb force.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines series connection?
o: a wiring in which the same current passes through every component one after another
a wiring in which the same voltage appears across every branch
the opposition inside a source that makes its terminal voltage fall as it delivers current
the energy supplied per unit charge by a source as it drives charge round a circuit
items.s: series connection: a wiring in which the same current passes through every component one after another. The other options describe internal resistance, parallel connection, electromotive force.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the condition in which a circuit carries more current than its components can safely bear”
o: overload
energy dissipated
joule heating
power rating
items.s: overload is the condition in which a circuit carries more current than its components can safely bear.

items.q: induced current is best described as
o: the production of a voltage in a coil by a change of the current in that same coil
a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence
the flow of charge set up in a closed loop by a changing magnetic flux
the production of a voltage in a conductor by a changing magnetic flux through it
items.s: induced current: the flow of charge set up in a closed loop by a changing magnetic flux. The other options describe self induction, eddy current, electromagnetic induction.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Direct current circuits?
o: ohm law of conduction
reactance
electric current
resistance
items.s: Every other option belongs to Direct current circuits. “reactance” belongs to Alternating current circuits, not Direct current circuits.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Wheatstone bridge?
o: the smallest change of the measured quantity that produces a detectable deflection
a four arm network balanced when the ratio of two pairs of resistances is equal
a practical form of balanced network using a one metre wire to find an unknown resistance
an instrument connected in the line of a circuit to measure the rate of charge flow
items.s: Wheatstone bridge: a four arm network balanced when the ratio of two pairs of resistances is equal. The other options describe meter bridge, ammeter, sensitivity of an instrument.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines conservation of charge.
o: a basic property of matter that makes a body attract or repel another and comes in two kinds
the rule that any observed amount of electricity on a body is a whole number multiple of the elementary amount
a charged body whose size is negligible compared with the distances in the problem
the principle that electricity can be neither created nor destroyed within an isolated region
items.s: conservation of charge: the principle that electricity can be neither created nor destroyed within an isolated region. The other options describe quantisation of charge, point charge, electric charge.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines series connection.
o: a wiring in which the same current passes through every component one after another
the resistance of a piece of material of unit length and unit cross section
a wiring in which the same voltage appears across every branch
the opposition a conductor offers to the flow of charge through it
items.s: series connection: a wiring in which the same current passes through every component one after another. The other options describe resistivity, parallel connection, resistance.

items.q: ohm law of conduction is best described as
o: the rate at which charge passes a given point in a circuit
the opposition a conductor offers to the flow of charge through it
the rule that the voltage across a conductor is proportional to the current through it at constant temperature
the opposition inside a source that makes its terminal voltage fall as it delivers current
items.s: ohm law of conduction: the rule that the voltage across a conductor is proportional to the current through it at constant temperature. The other options describe internal resistance, resistance, electric current.

items.q: Which of the following best describes equipotential surface?
o: the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to a point
a region in which the electric push has the same magnitude and direction at every point
the rate at which the energy per unit charge changes with distance along a direction
a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge
items.s: equipotential surface: a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge. The other options describe electric potential, uniform field, potential gradient.

items.q: Which term is described by “a charged body whose size is negligible compared with the distances in the problem”?
o: permittivity
charging by induction
point charge
electrostatic shielding
items.s: point charge is a charged body whose size is negligible compared with the distances in the problem.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the production of heat in a conductor by the passage of current through its resistance”
o: efficiency of a source
power rating
overload
joule heating
items.s: joule heating is the production of heat in a conductor by the passage of current through its resistance.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Alternating current circuits?
o: root mean square value
alternating current
cyclotron motion
peak value
items.s: Every other option belongs to Alternating current circuits. “cyclotron motion” belongs to Force on a current in a magnetic field, not Alternating current circuits.

items.q: Which term is described by “a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence”?
o: magnetic flux linkage
self induction
eddy current
Faraday law of induction
items.s: eddy current is a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence.

items.q: meter bridge is best described as
o: a four arm network balanced when the ratio of two pairs of resistances is equal
a practical form of balanced network using a one metre wire to find an unknown resistance
a uniform wire and sliding contact used to compare voltages without drawing current from the source being measured
a high resistance placed in series with an instrument to extend the range of voltage it can read
items.s: meter bridge: a practical form of balanced network using a one metre wire to find an unknown resistance. The other options describe Wheatstone bridge, potentiometer, multiplier.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Magnetic field of a current?
o: potential difference
tesla
magnetic field
magnetic flux density
items.s: Every other option belongs to Magnetic field of a current. “potential difference” belongs to Electric field and potential, not Magnetic field of a current.

items.q: electric field intensity is best described as
o: a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge
a region in which the electric push has the same magnitude and direction at every point
the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to a point
the push per unit positive charge experienced at a point in a region of electrical influence
items.s: electric field intensity: the push per unit positive charge experienced at a point in a region of electrical influence. The other options describe uniform field, equipotential surface, electric potential.

items.q: cyclotron motion is best described as
o: the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region
a convention relating the directions of push, flux density and current for a conductor placed across a magnetic region
the circular path followed by a charged particle entering a magnetic region at right angles
the combined push on a charge moving in regions of electric and magnetic influence
items.s: cyclotron motion: the circular path followed by a charged particle entering a magnetic region at right angles. The other options describe Fleming left hand rule, Lorentz force, torque on a coil.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines magnetic field.
o: a region in which a moving charge or a magnet experiences a sideways push
the force acting per unit length on a wire carrying unit current at right angles to the region
the flux density in which a wire carrying one ampere experiences one newton per metre of its length
the property of a medium that measures how readily it supports a magnetic influence
items.s: magnetic field: a region in which a moving charge or a magnet experiences a sideways push. The other options describe tesla, permeability, magnetic flux density.

items.q: Which term is described by “a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the electric push there”?
o: equipotential surface
electric field intensity
field line
uniform field
items.s: field line is a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the electric push there.

items.q: Which of the following best describes farad?
o: the amount of charge a conductor holds per unit rise of its energy per unit charge
the work accumulated in a charged device, equal to half the product of its capacitance and the square of the voltage
the capacitance of a conductor that holds one coulomb when its energy per unit charge rises by one volt
the slow loss of stored charge through an imperfect insulator
items.s: farad: the capacitance of a conductor that holds one coulomb when its energy per unit charge rises by one volt. The other options describe capacitance, energy stored in a capacitor, leakage.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines electrostatic shielding.
o: the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material
a basic property of matter that makes a body attract or repel another and comes in two kinds
the rule that any observed amount of electricity on a body is a whole number multiple of the elementary amount
the transfer of charge to a conductor without any contact, by bringing a charged body near it
items.s: electrostatic shielding: the blocking of electric influence from a region by enclosing it in a conducting material. The other options describe electric charge, charging by induction, quantisation of charge.

items.q: multiplier is best described as
o: an instrument connected in the line of a circuit to measure the rate of charge flow
a four arm network balanced when the ratio of two pairs of resistances is equal
a high resistance placed in series with an instrument to extend the range of voltage it can read
the smallest change of the measured quantity that produces a detectable deflection
items.s: multiplier: a high resistance placed in series with an instrument to extend the range of voltage it can read. The other options describe Wheatstone bridge, ammeter, sensitivity of an instrument.

items.q: electromagnetic induction is best described as
o: the rule that the induced voltage equals the rate of change of flux linkage
the rule that an induced current flows in the direction that opposes the change producing it
the production of a voltage in a conductor by a changing magnetic flux through it
a circulating flow of electricity set up in the body of a solid conductor by a changing magnetic influence
items.s: electromagnetic induction: the production of a voltage in a conductor by a changing magnetic flux through it. The other options describe Faraday law of induction, Lenz law, eddy current.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines velocity selector.
o: a convention relating the directions of push, flux density and current for a conductor placed across a magnetic region
an arrangement of crossed electric and magnetic regions that lets only particles of one speed pass straight through
the sideways push experienced by electricity in motion across a magnetic region
the circular path followed by a charged particle entering a magnetic region at right angles
items.s: velocity selector: an arrangement of crossed electric and magnetic regions that lets only particles of one speed pass straight through. The other options describe cyclotron motion, force on a moving charge, Fleming left hand rule.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: Which term is described by “a wiring in which the same voltage appears across every branch”?
o: internal resistance
ohm law of conduction
parallel connection
resistance
items.s: parallel connection is a wiring in which the same voltage appears across every branch.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition in which a circuit carries more current than its components can safely bear”?
o: electrical power
overload
joule heating
efficiency of a source
items.s: overload is the condition in which a circuit carries more current than its components can safely bear.

items.q: Which of the following best describes energy dissipated?
o: the condition in which a circuit carries more current than its components can safely bear
the rate of energy transfer a device is designed to handle safely
the ratio of the energy delivered to the load to the total energy generated
the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component
items.s: energy dissipated: the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component. The other options describe power rating, efficiency of a source, overload.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines potential gradient.
o: a curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the electric push there
the rate at which the energy per unit charge changes with distance along a direction
a set of points all at the same value of electrical energy per unit charge
the push per unit positive charge experienced at a point in a region of electrical influence
items.s: potential gradient: the rate at which the energy per unit charge changes with distance along a direction. The other options describe equipotential surface, field line, electric field intensity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes permittivity?
o: the transfer of charge to a conductor without any contact, by bringing a charged body near it
the property of a medium that measures how readily it allows an electric influence to pass through it
the principle that electricity can be neither created nor destroyed within an isolated region
the rule that the push between two point charges varies as the product of the charges and inversely as the squared separation
items.s: permittivity: the property of a medium that measures how readily it allows an electric influence to pass through it. The other options describe Coulomb law of force, charging by induction, conservation of charge.

items.q: Which of the following best describes quantisation of charge?
o: the property of a medium that measures how readily it allows an electric influence to pass through it
the rule that the push between two point charges varies as the product of the charges and inversely as the squared separation
a charged body whose size is negligible compared with the distances in the problem
the rule that any observed amount of electricity on a body is a whole number multiple of the elementary amount
items.s: quantisation of charge: the rule that any observed amount of electricity on a body is a whole number multiple of the elementary amount. The other options describe point charge, Coulomb law of force, permittivity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes magnetic field line?
o: a long coil of insulated wire that produces a nearly uniform magnetic region inside it
the flux density in which a wire carrying one ampere experiences one newton per metre of its length
a region in which a moving charge or a magnet experiences a sideways push
a closed curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the push due to a magnet or a current
items.s: magnetic field line: a closed curve whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the push due to a magnet or a current. The other options describe tesla, solenoid, magnetic field.

items.q: capacitance is best described as
o: two flat conducting sheets facing each other with an insulator between them, used to store charge
the constant appearing in the law of force between charges in a vacuum
the amount of charge a conductor holds per unit rise of its energy per unit charge

the energy supplied per unit charge by a source as it drives charge round a circuit
