the rate at which a circuit transfers energy, equal to the product of voltage and current
the component or network that receives energy from a source
the rate of energy transfer a device is designed to handle safely

a convention relating the directions of push, flux density and current for a conductor placed across a magnetic region
the turning effect produced on a loop carrying current when its plane lies along a magnetic region

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines magnetic field line.

a long coil of insulated wire that produces a nearly uniform magnetic region inside it
a substance such as iron that greatly concentrates the magnetic influence passing through it

the flow of charge set up in a closed loop by a changing magnetic flux
the production of a voltage in a conductor by a changing magnetic flux through it

electrostatic shielding
alternating current

the work accumulated in a charged device, equal to half the product of its capacitance and the square of the voltage

items.q: A coil of 50 turns and area 0.05 m squared carries a current of 4 A with its plane along a magnetic field of flux density 0.8 T. Calculate the turning effect on the coil in N m.

items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A series circuit contains an inductance of 0.2 H and a capacitance of 100 microfarad. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its resonant frequency in Hz.
items.s: At resonance the frequency is 1 / (2 pi x square root of inductance x capacitance) = 35.58 Hz.

items.q: A circuit draws a root mean square current of 4 A from a 100 V root mean square supply at a power factor of 0.8. Calculate the true power consumed in W.
items.s: True power = voltage x current x power factor = 100 x 4 x 0.8 = 320 W.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 10 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.1 A. Calculate the shunt needed to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 3 A, in ohm.
items.s: The shunt carries the excess current, so its value is 10 x 0.1 / (3 - 0.1) = 0.3448 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 100 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.001 A. Calculate the series resistance needed to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to 20 V, in ohm.
items.s: The series resistance must drop the remaining voltage, so its value is 20 / 0.001 - 100 = 19900 ohm.

items.q: Two point charges attract each other with a force of 20 N when they are a certain distance apart. Calculate the force in N when the separation is increased to 4 times its original value.
items.s: The force varies inversely as the square of the separation, so the new force is 20 divided by 4 x 4 = 1.25 N.

items.q: Two point charges of 3 microcoulomb and 10 microcoulomb are placed 0.4 m apart in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the force between them in N.
items.s: Force = constant x product of the charges / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 3 x 10^-6 x 10 x 10^-6 / (0.4 x 0.4) = 1.69 N.

items.q: A small body carries a charge of 20 electronic charges. Taking the elementary charge as 1.6 x 10^-19 C, calculate the charge on the body in units of 10^-19 C.
items.s: Charge = number of elementary charges x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 20 x 1.6 = 32 units of 10^-19 C.

items.q: A point charge of 6 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.2 m from it in kV/m.
items.s: Field intensity = constant x charge / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 6 x 10^-6 / (0.2 x 0.2) = 1350 kV/m.

items.q: A point charge of 4 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric potential 0.2 m from it in kV.
items.s: Potential = constant x charge / distance = 9.0 x 10^9 x 4 x 10^-6 / 0.2 = 180 kV.

items.q: Two parallel plates 0.2 m apart carry a uniform electric field of 400 V/m between them. Calculate the potential difference between the plates in V.
items.s: Potential difference = field intensity x separation = 400 x 0.2 = 80 V.

items.q: A charge of 8 microcoulomb is moved between two points whose potential difference is 200 V. Calculate the work done in mJ.
items.s: Work done = charge x potential difference = 8 x 10^-6 x 200 = 1.6 mJ.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 40 microfarad is connected across a 240 V supply. Calculate the charge stored on it in microcoulomb.
items.s: Charge stored = capacitance x voltage = 40 x 10^-6 x 240 = 9600 microcoulomb.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 25 microfarad is charged to 250 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.
items.s: Energy stored = half the capacitance times the voltage squared = 0.5 x 25 x 10^-6 x 250 x 250 = 781.2 mJ.

items.q: Two capacitors of 3 microfarad and 4 microfarad are connected in series. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination in microfarad.
items.s: For capacitors in series the reciprocals add, so the equivalent capacitance is 3 x 4 / (3 + 4) = 1.71 microfarad.

items.q: Three capacitors of 4 microfarad, 5 microfarad and 10 microfarad are joined in parallel. Calculate the equivalent capacitance in microfarad.
items.s: Capacitors in parallel add directly, so the equivalent capacitance is 4 + 5 + 10 = 19 microfarad.

items.q: A resistor of 2 ohm is connected across a 120 V supply of negligible internal resistance. Calculate the current through it in A.
items.s: Current = voltage / resistance = 120 / 2 = 60 A.

items.q: Resistors of 20 ohm, 15 ohm and 8 ohm are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistances in series add directly, so the total is 20 + 15 + 8 = 43 ohm.

items.q: Two resistors of 6 ohm and 24 ohm are connected in parallel. Calculate their combined resistance in ohm.
items.s: For two resistors in parallel the combined value is 6 x 24 / (6 + 24) = 4.8 ohm.

items.q: A cell of electromotive force 9 V and internal resistance 0.2 ohm delivers a current of 1 A. Calculate its terminal potential difference in V.
items.s: Terminal voltage = electromotive force - current x internal resistance = 9 - 1 x 0.2 = 8.8 V.

items.q: A wire of length 4 m and cross sectional area 0.5 x 10^-6 m squared is made of a material of resistivity 2.8 x 10^-8 ohm m. Calculate its resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistance = resistivity x length / area = 2.8 x 10^-8 x 4 / (0.5 x 10^-6) = 0.224 ohm.

items.q: A current of 2 A divides between two parallel resistors of 10 ohm and 12 ohm. Calculate the current through the 10 ohm resistor in A.
items.s: The current divides in inverse proportion to the resistances, so through the 10 ohm branch it is 2 x 12 / (10 + 12) = 1.09 A.

items.q: A device draws a current of 1.5 A from a 24 V supply. Calculate the power it consumes in W.
items.s: Power = voltage x current = 24 x 1.5 = 36 W.

items.q: A current of 5 A flows through a resistor of 5 ohm. Calculate the rate at which heat is produced in it in W.
items.s: Rate of heating = current squared x resistance = 5 x 5 x 5 = 125 W.

items.q: An appliance rated 2000 W is used for 2 hours. Calculate the energy it consumes in kWh.
items.s: Energy = power x time = 2000 W x 2 h = 4 kWh after dividing by one thousand.

items.q: A heater rated 1000 W runs for 6 hours each day. If electrical energy costs 20 naira per kWh, calculate the daily cost in naira.
items.s: The daily energy is 1000 x 6 / 1000 = 6 kWh, so the cost is 6 x 20 = 120 naira.

items.q: A flat surface of area 0.1 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 1 T. Calculate the magnetic flux through the surface in Wb.
items.s: Flux = flux density x area for a surface at right angles = 1 x 0.1 = 0.1 Wb.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current of 10 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the magnetic flux density 0.1 m from the wire in microtesla.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x current / (2 pi x distance) = 20 microtesla.

items.q: A solenoid of length 0.25 m has 2000 turns and carries a current of 5 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density near its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density = permeability x turns per metre x current = 50.27 mT.

items.q: A straight wire of length 0.2 m carries a current of 2 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.25 T. Calculate the force on the wire in N.
items.s: Force = flux density x current x length = 0.25 x 2 x 0.2 = 0.1 N.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A particle carrying 1 microcoulomb moves at 2 x 10^6 m/s at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T. Calculate the magnetic force on it in N.
items.s: Force = charge x speed x flux density for motion at right angles = 1 x 10^-6 x 2 x 10^6 x 0.5 = 1 N.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A coil of 200 turns and area 0.05 m squared lies at right angles to a magnetic field that changes uniformly from 0 T to 1 T in 0.2 s. Calculate the average voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = turns x change of flux density x area / time = 200 x 1 x 0.05 / 0.2 = 50 V.

items.q: A transformer has 400 turns in its primary and 20 turns in its secondary. If the primary is connected to a 220 V supply, calculate the secondary voltage in V.
items.s: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, so the secondary voltage is 220 x 20 / 400 = 11 V.

items.q: An ideal transformer has 400 primary turns and 50 secondary turns and the primary current is 4 A. Calculate the secondary current in A.
items.s: For an ideal transformer the current ratio is the inverse of the turns ratio, so the secondary current is 4 x 400 / 50 = 32 A.

items.q: The current in a coil of inductance 0.4 H changes steadily by 2 A in 0.1 s. Calculate the voltage induced in the coil in V.
items.s: Induced voltage = inductance x rate of change of current = 0.4 x 2 / 0.1 = 8 V.

items.q: A capacitor of 50 microfarad is connected to a 100 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its capacitive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Capacitive reactance = 1 / (2 pi x frequency x capacitance) = 1 / (2 x 3.142 x 100 x 50 x 10^-6) = 31.83 ohm.

items.q: A coil of inductance 2 H is connected to a 100 Hz supply. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its inductive reactance in ohm.
items.s: Inductive reactance = 2 pi x frequency x inductance = 2 x 3.142 x 100 x 2 = 1257 ohm.

items.q: A series circuit contains a resistance of 8 ohm and a reactance of 12 ohm. Calculate its impedance in ohm.
items.s: Impedance is the square root of the sum of the squares = sqrt(8 x 8 + 12 x 12) = 14.42 ohm.

items.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge the first arm is 5 ohm, the second is 4 ohm and the third is 24 ohm. Calculate the resistance of the fourth arm in ohm.
items.s: At balance the ratio of the first two arms equals the ratio of the last two, so the fourth arm is 4 x 24 / 5 = 19.2 ohm.

items.q: A metre bridge balances with a resistance of 12 ohm in the left gap and a balance length of 65 cm from the left end. Calculate the unknown resistance in the right gap in ohm.
items.s: The unknown equals the known resistance times the balance length divided by the remaining length = 12 x 65 / 35 = 22.29 ohm.

items.q: A circular coil of 50 turns and radius 0.25 m carries a current of 3 A. Taking the permeability of free space as 4 pi x 10^-7 T m/A, calculate the flux density at its centre in mT.
items.s: Flux density at the centre = permeability x turns x current / (2 x radius) = 0.377 mT.

items.q: A coil of 100 turns and area 0.01 m squared carries a current of 1.5 A with its plane along a magnetic field of flux density 0.8 T. Calculate the turning effect on the coil in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = turns x current x area x flux density = 100 x 1.5 x 0.01 x 0.8 = 1.2 N m.
items.t: Force on a current in a magnetic field

items.q: A series circuit contains an inductance of 0.5 H and a capacitance of 25 microfarad. Taking pi as 3.142, calculate its resonant frequency in Hz.
items.s: At resonance the frequency is 1 / (2 pi x square root of inductance x capacitance) = 45.01 Hz.

items.q: A circuit draws a root mean square current of 3 A from a 200 V root mean square supply at a power factor of 0.85. Calculate the true power consumed in W.
items.s: True power = voltage x current x power factor = 200 x 3 x 0.85 = 510 W.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 80 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.01 A. Calculate the shunt needed to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 2 A, in ohm.
items.s: The shunt carries the excess current, so its value is 80 x 0.01 / (2 - 0.01) = 0.402 ohm.

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 ohm gives a full scale deflection for 0.005 A. Calculate the series resistance needed to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to 50 V, in ohm.
items.s: The series resistance must drop the remaining voltage, so its value is 50 / 0.005 - 50 = 9950 ohm.

items.q: Two point charges of 8 microcoulomb and 5 microcoulomb are placed 0.4 m apart in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the force between them in N.
items.s: Force = constant x product of the charges / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 8 x 10^-6 x 5 x 10^-6 / (0.4 x 0.4) = 2.25 N.

items.q: A point charge of 5 microcoulomb is isolated in a vacuum. Taking the Coulomb constant as 9.0 x 10^9 N m squared per C squared, calculate the electric field intensity 0.4 m from it in kV/m.
items.s: Field intensity = constant x charge / distance squared = 9.0 x 10^9 x 5 x 10^-6 / (0.4 x 0.4) = 281.2 kV/m.

items.q: Two parallel plates 0.01 m apart carry a uniform electric field of 200 V/m between them. Calculate the potential difference between the plates in V.
items.s: Potential difference = field intensity x separation = 200 x 0.01 = 2 V.

items.q: A charge of 8 microcoulomb is moved between two points whose potential difference is 100 V. Calculate the work done in mJ.
items.s: Work done = charge x potential difference = 8 x 10^-6 x 100 = 0.8 mJ.

items.q: A capacitor of capacitance 10 microfarad is charged to 100 V. Calculate the energy stored in it in mJ.
items.s: Energy stored = half the capacitance times the voltage squared = 0.5 x 10 x 10^-6 x 100 x 100 = 50 mJ.

items.q: Two capacitors of 2 microfarad and 24 microfarad are connected in series. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination in microfarad.
items.s: For capacitors in series the reciprocals add, so the equivalent capacitance is 2 x 24 / (2 + 24) = 1.85 microfarad.

items.q: Three capacitors of 6 microfarad, 15 microfarad and 20 microfarad are joined in parallel. Calculate the equivalent capacitance in microfarad.
items.s: Capacitors in parallel add directly, so the equivalent capacitance is 6 + 15 + 20 = 41 microfarad.

items.q: A resistor of 15 ohm is connected across a 120 V supply of negligible internal resistance. Calculate the current through it in A.

items.q: Resistors of 8 ohm, 15 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in ohm.

items.q: Two resistors of 6 ohm and 4 ohm are connected in parallel. Calculate their combined resistance in ohm.

items.q: A cell of electromotive force 9 V and internal resistance 0.2 ohm delivers a current of 2 A. Calculate its terminal potential difference in V.
items.s: Terminal voltage = electromotive force - current x internal resistance = 9 - 2 x 0.2 = 8.6 V.

items.q: A wire of length 3 m and cross sectional area 1 x 10^-6 m squared is made of a material of resistivity 11 x 10^-8 ohm m. Calculate its resistance in ohm.
items.s: Resistance = resistivity x length / area = 11 x 10^-8 x 3 / (1 x 10^-6) = 0.33 ohm.

items.q: A current of 6 A divides between two parallel resistors of 2 ohm and 12 ohm. Calculate the current through the 2 ohm resistor in A.
items.s: The current divides in inverse proportion to the resistances, so through the 2 ohm branch it is 6 x 12 / (2 + 12) = 5.14 A.

items.q: A device draws a current of 5 A from a 50 V supply. Calculate the power it consumes in W.

items.q: “the electrical work converted into heat or other forms in a component” is the definition of

load
